q: Which of the following statements about the Ajanta caves is correct?
options: The Vaghoda panel in Cave 1 of the Ajanta shows the Padmapani Bodhisattva
explanation: The Vaghoda panel of the Cave 1 of the Ajanta, painted in the sixth century CE, is the finest of the Indian murals and it shows the Bodhisattva Padmapani.

q: The 'Kailasanatha temple' at Kanchipuram was built by:
explanation: The Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram was built by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I as a replica of the Kailasa temple of the Ellora, which was cut in the rock.

q: Kanchi Kailasanatha is:
options: a structural temple of the Cholas
a rock-cut temple in imitation of the Ellora Kailasa
explanation: The Kailasanatha temple of Kanchipuram was an imitation in stone of the rock-cut Kailasa temple of the Ellora, and it was built by the Narasimhavarman I.

q: The Mandapas of the Mahabalipuram are:
options: the rock-cut monuments of the Pallavas
the structural temples of the Cholas
the Jain temples of the medieval period
explanation: The Mandapas, the rock-cut monuments of Mahabalipuram, are the works of the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I and they include the famous Trimurti cave.

q: The 'Trimurti' at Mahabalipuram:
options: Is a temple of the Vijayanagara
Is the rock-cut panel of Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma in one face
explanation: The Trimurti cave of Mahabalipuram shows the three faces of Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma in a single rock panel, and the panel is protected by a later shrine.

q: The 'Brihadisvara temple' at Thanjavur:
options: Is the Chola temple of Rajaraja I with the 66 metre tall vimana
It is a temple of the Nayaks
explanation: The Brihadisvara temple at Thanjavur, built by the Chola king Rajaraja I between 1003 and 1010, has a 66 metre tall vimana and it is a World Heritage site.

q: The 'Airavatesvara temple' at Darasuram:
options: Is the Chola temple of Rajaraja II with the frescoes
explanation: The Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram, built by the Chola king Rajaraja II, is remarkable for its stone frescoes and the high quality of its sculpture.

q: The 'Gangaikonda Cholapuram' temple:
options: Is the temple of the Cholas built by Rajendra I and completed by Kulothunga I
Is the temple of Rajaraja I
explanation: The Gangaikonda Cholapuram temple was built by the Chola emperor Rajendra I and it was completed by his successor Kulothunga I with the victory columns.

q: The temples at Khajuraho are:
options: the Chandela monuments of the 10th and 11th centuries
explanation: The temples at Khajuraho were built by the Chandela rulers of Bundelkhand in the tenth and the eleventh centuries and the erotic sculptures are a celebration of the life.

q: The Konark Sun Temple of the Odisha is:
options: the Kalinga style temple of Narasimhadeva I shaped like a chariot
a Dravidian temple of the Vijayanagara
explanation: The Konark temple, built under the Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I, is shaped like a giant chariot of the sun god with the wheels and the horses and the warriors carved around it.

q: The 'Sun Temple' at Modhera was built by:
explanation: The Sun temple at Modhera in Gujarat was built in the eleventh century by the Solanki king Bhima I and it is a World Heritage site.

q: The Bada Gumbad at Bijapur is:
options: It is a mosque at Ahmedabad
It is a tomb at Golconda
Is the tomb of the Bahmani or the Adil Shahi at Bijapur
explanation: The Bada Gumbad, the largest monument of the Bijapur, is the tomb of the Adil Shahi or the Bahmani ruler and it is a World Heritage site.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Ibrahim Adil Shah II is correct?
explanation: The Gol Gumbaz, the mausoleum of the Adil Shahi dynasty, was built by the Ibrahim Adil Shah II in 1656 and it houses the tomb of the Rohilla Gaur.

q: The 'Ibrahim Rauza' at Bijapur:
options: Is the tomb of the Ibrahim Adil Shah II and the finest of the Adil Shahi tombs
explanation: The Ibrahim Rauza, built in 1620, is the tomb of the Ibrahim Adil Shah II and it is considered the finest of the Adil Shahi monuments with the exquisite decorations.

q: The Charminar monument at Hyderabad is:
options: Is the monument of the Qutb Shahi with four minarets and it was built in 1591
It is a temple of the Vijayanagara
explanation: The Charminar, built in 1591 by the Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, has the four minarets and it marks the centre of the new city of Hyderabad.

q: The Qutb Shahi dynasty of the Deccan is:
options: The Qutb Shahi capital was Bijapur
The Qutb Shahi ruled at Ahmedabad
The Qutb Shahi were a Mughal clan
The Qutb Shahi had their capital at Golconda with the famous Golconda mines of the diamonds
explanation: The Qutb Shahi dynasty ruled at Golconda near Hyderabad from 1518 and the Golconda mines produced the famous diamonds, including the Koh-i-Noor, that were traded through the Portuguese at Goa.

q: The 'Tomb of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah':
options: Is the earliest surviving monument of the Qutb Shahi at Hyderabad
explanation: The tomb of the Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah is the earliest surviving Qutb Shahi monument at Hyderabad and it has the ruins of a mosque and a later Golconda-style mosque in the complex.

q: The Bara Imambara at Lucknow is:
options: It is a Jain pilgrimage centre
Is the Asafi mosque of the Lucknow built by the Nawab Saadat Ali Khan II
It is a temple of the Vijayanagara
It is a monument of the Mughals
explanation: The Bara Imambara, the Asafi mosque of the Lucknow built by the Nawab Saadat Ali Khan II after the famine of 1784, is the largest of the Asafis of the city.

q: The Itimad-ud-Daulah tomb of the Agra is:
options: at Agra and is the first Mughal monument in the white marble
explanation: The tomb of the Itimad-ud-Daulah at Agra, built by the Nur Jahan for her father, is the first Mughal monument constructed entirely of the white marble.

q: Tomb of Safdarjung is:
options: at Delhi and was designed by the Jean-Baptiste Tavernier for the Safdarjung
explanation: The tomb of the Safdarjung at Delhi was built in 1753 for the Nawab Safdarjung and it was designed by the French architect, the Jean-Baptiste Tavernier.

q: The Red Fort at Delhi is:
options: Is a fort of the Rajasthan
Is the Lal Qila of Delhi built by the Akbar and completed by the Shah Jahan
explanation: The Red Fort, called the Lal Qila, was built by the Akbar between 1638 and 1648 and it was completed by the Shah Jahan and it is a World Heritage site.

q: The 'Fatehpur Sikri':
options: Is the Mughal capital built by the Akbar in 1571
Is the capital of the Mughals in 1648
It is a temple of the Sikhs
It is a fort of the British
explanation: The Fatehpur Sikri, the Mughal capital from 1571 to 1585, was built by the Akbar and it is noted for the Buland Darwaza and the tomb of the Salim Chishti.

q: The 'Jama Masjid' of Fatehpur Sikri:
options: Is the largest of the Mughal mosque with the Jai Mandir of the Akbar
Is the mosque of the Shah Jahan
explanation: The Jama Masjid of Fatehpur Sikri, with the Jai Mandir of the Akbar adjoining it, is the largest of the individual Mughal mosque complexes.

q: The 'Humayun's Tomb':
options: It is the tomb of the Akbar
Is the first Mughal monument of the white marble and was designed by the Mirak Mirza Ghiyas
It was designed by the Sinan
explanation: The tomb of the Humayun, designed by the Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas, is the first of the grand Mughal tombs in Delhi and it is a precursor of the Taj Mahal.

q: The 'Tomb of Akbar' at Sikandra:
options: Is the largest of the Mughal tombs in India with the high entrance gateway
explanation: The tomb of the Akbar at Sikandra near Agra, completed by the Jahangir, is the largest of the Mughal tombs in India with the tall southern entrance gateway.

q: The Moti Masjid in the Red Fort at Delhi is:
options: Is the mosque of the Shah Jahan in the Red Fort built of the white marble
It is the mosque of the Akbar
It is a temple of the Rajputs
explanation: The Moti Masjid, the Pearl Mosque of the Shah Jahan, is in the Red Fort complex and it is built of the white marble with the red sandstone of the fort.

q: Was built by the Shah Jahan and it is:
options: the largest of the Indian mosques
explanation: The Jama Masjid of Delhi was built by the Shah Jahan between 1650 and 1656 and it can hold about 25,000 worshippers and it is the largest of the Indian mosques.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Qutbuddin Aibak and completed is correct?
options: Qutbuddin Aibak and completed by Iltutmish
explanation: The Qutb Minar, the red sandstone minaret of the Qutb complex in Delhi, was begun by the Qutbuddin Aibak and completed by his son Iltutmish with the addition of the top storey.

q: The 'Iron Pillar' of Delhi:
options: It is of the Mughal period
It is of the British period
Is a testament to the corrosion resistance of the iron of the 5th century
explanation: The Iron Pillar of the Qutb complex, of the fifth century, shows the remarkable corrosion resistance of the iron and it is a World Heritage site as a part of the Qutb complex.

q: The 'Alai Darwaza' was built by:
explanation: The Alai Darwaza, the gateway of the Alai Minar of the Qutb complex in Delhi, was built by the Alauddin Khalji.

q: Firoz Shah Kotla is:
options: the citadel of the Tughlaq in Delhi with the Ashokan pillars and the Jantar Mantar of the Jai Singh II
explanation: The Firoz Shah Kotla, the citadel of the Tughlaq in Delhi, has the Ashokan pillars and the Jantar Mantar, the observatory of the Jai Singh II.

q: The 'Purana Qila' of Delhi:
options: Is the old fort of the Humayun and the Sher Mandal
It is a fort of the Akbar
explanation: The Purana Qila, the old fort of Delhi, was built by the Humayun and it houses the Sher Mandal, the tower from which the Shah Jahan is said to have first seen the Taj Mahal.

q: The Ashokan pillars at Feroz Shah Kotla in Delhi are:
options: Two of the Ashokan pillars stand at the Feroz Shah Kotla in Delhi
explanation: Two of the Ashokan pillars, one from the Topra in the Haryana and the other from the Meerut, were brought by the Firoz Shah Tughlaq to Delhi and they stand at the Firoz Shah Kotla.
